        <section class="about-intro">
          <div class="section-label">About the portfolio</div>
          <h2>A little about me</h2>
          <p>I am Prasanga Paudel, a PhD student in Agriculture and Applied Economics at Texas Tech University, with a growing interest in the intersection of economics, data, technology, and real-world decision making. My academic work has given me a strong foundation in economic theory, econometrics, statistics, and applied research, while my projects have pushed me to think more broadly about how data can be organized, analyzed, visualized, and communicated. This portfolio is a place where those interests come together.</p>
          <p>My work is rooted in applied economics, particularly questions involving economic behavior, public policy, environmental issues, energy, agriculture, and individual decision making. I have worked with survey experiments, willingness-to-pay estimation, econometric analysis, and policy-oriented research. I enjoy taking a broad question, turning it into something measurable, developing an empirical strategy, and using data to understand what the results actually tell us.</p>
          <p>R and Quarto have been important parts of that development. I have used R for statistical and econometric analysis, data manipulation, visualization, and reproducible research, and I built this portfolio using Quarto. I have also started using Python for visualization and data-related projects. My next goal is to become comfortable moving between languages depending on the problem: R for statistical work, Python for data science and broader programming, and eventually C++ and Java for deeper computational and programming skills.</p>
          <p>This website reflects that transition. Some sections contain work I have already completed, while others are placeholders for projects I will build in the future. I want the portfolio to show progression rather than pretend that every skill is already mastered. The programming section will eventually contain separate areas for Python, R, C++, and Java, while the project section will organize work by areas such as economics, finance, data science, and visualization.</p>
          <p>I also care about presentation. Good quantitative work should be understandable to someone who did not write the code that produced it. Visualization and communication are therefore important parts of the way I approach projects. I want to build dashboards and visual explanations that make quantitative information easier to explore without hiding the underlying complexity.</p>
          <p>Ultimately, this portfolio is a work in progress. My academic background is in agriculture and applied economics, but I see data and programming as increasingly important tools for working across disciplines. I want to keep building projects that combine economic reasoning, careful empirical analysis, useful visualization, and reproducible code. As I learn new languages and techniques, this site will grow with me.</p>
        </section>
